SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
Sherri Juby Clark’S INITIAL brief
Intervenor Sherri Juby Clark files this Initial Brief in the above-styled and numbered docket. The intervenor number for these landowners in Egnyte is 315.
In summary, my property is on Link G2, and I am opposed to any route that uses Link G2, Link G13, or Link G6 for the reasons set forth below.
90% or nineteen landowners on Link G2 filed written testimony that was admitted into evidence. This is an extremely high percentage of the affected properties on Link G2. This alone is strong evidence of the opposition to Link G2 by our rural community.
But there are more substantive reasons that Link G2 should not be used.
The installation of the Matterhorn gas pipeline in 2024 on my property, combined with the upcoming Eiger Express expansion, already subjects our property to a 100-foot-wide utility easement. Adding a third major project—a high-voltage transmission line—imposes a disproportionate and unreasonable burden on a single private landowner. see 315-Sherri Clark, Admitted Exhibits – S. Clark Direct Testimony 5-12-26.docx, Exhibit E, page 9
The proposed G2 link runs in close proximity to high-hazard facilities such as Firefly’s Rocket Ranch rocket engine testing facility, which experienced a large fireball explosion from a rocket booster malfunction on September 29th, 2005. There is a history of volatility here. Introducing a high-voltage electrical infrastructure next to an active rocket propulsion testing site creates an unacceptable risk. A secondary incident involving power lines during a facility malfunction could create a localized disaster. see 357-Samuel Eaton, Admitted Exhibits – EXH_002_firefely_explosion.pdf
The Matterhorn and Eiger Gas Pipelines run in front of Firefly’s Rocket Ranch facility, creating a concentration of industrial infrastructure as the G2 link would cross the gas pipelines if constructed. Co-locating high-voltage electrical lines over major high-pressure natural gas pipelines next to an aerospace testing facility creates a dense “hazard zone.” see 313-Brian Smith, Admitted Exhibits – Brian J Smith - Exhibit 1.pdf (Brian J Smith Direct Testimony), Exhibit D, page 9
The Briggs area where the G2 link would cross has a history of dangerous and unpredictable weather patterns – as tornadoes swept the area in May 2025. This adds to the level of danger by increasing the risk of live, high-voltage wires snapping and falling onto populated areas that already host large-scale gas pipelines, creating hazards and sparking fast-moving fires amidst existing storm damage. see 357-G31 Landowners, Admitted Exhibits – EXH_006_Tornados_May 2025.pdf
Our local fire station near the proposed G2 link has an active helipad used for Careflight Operations – the G2 link could interfere with emergency flight paths or operations. Constructing massive transmission towers and high-voltage lines in this immediate vicinity creates permanent, deadly aerial obstructions. Any interference with emergency flight paths or active air-ambulance operations directly jeopardizes public safety and delays critical, life-saving medical transports when minutes matter most. see 315-Sherri Clark, Admitted Exhibits – S. Clark Direct Testimony 5-12-26.docx, Exhibit C, page 7
Link G13 (which connects with Link G2) had all but one landowner intervene and file testimony. The overwhelming participation of both G2 and G13 landowners attests to the strong community values and the negative impact these lines would have on the rural nature of the Briggs community. see 335-G9 and G13 Landowners, Admitted Exhibits – G9 and G13 Landowners Exhibit 1-59475 Direct Testimony of Thomas Ghidossi, page 8 of 46, lines 6 through 9
My family has been the sole stewards of this land since the Texas Land Rush of 1881. Placing an industrial transmission corridor on this land completely disrespects a 145-year legacy of unbroken family stewardship dating back to 1881, permanently scarring a piece of living Texas history that should be preserved, not industrialized.

In conclusion, for the reasons stated above, I oppose any route using Link G2, Link G13, 
or Link G6.
	Respectfully submitted,
	Sherri Juby Clark
